themes.title: The humanoid platform race
themes.description: Nvidia was reportedly weighing another ~$1B into Figure at a ~$38B pre-money valuation (unconfirmed, Oct 8), while Barron's questions Optimus' commercial progress. Tesla reports Oct 21 and investors want Optimus operating evidence. South Korea (Oct 13) approved a sandbox trial of 20 Robros humanoids at four firms, and UBTech has admitted Walker S2 reaches only 30–50% of human productivity.

themes.title: Reshoring keeps the automation base humming
themes.description: Teradyne last traded ~$403 (Oct 10) after a ~200% 12-month run; Rockwell held near $450s. Fanuc reports Oct 22. Cognex agreed to buy RealSense for $500M (Sept), adding 3D vision depth sensing for robots.

themes.title: Warehouse automation is already profitable
themes.description: Symbotic's ~$22.5B backlog is >30x quarterly revenue and it added German sortation firm cellumation; consensus targets (~$62.86) sat ~45% above its ~$43 price (Oct 10) yet the stock is down ~33% YTD. Warehouse robotics is paid for at scale, but sentiment lags.

themes.title: Da Vinci's monopoly is ending
themes.description: J&J's Ottava (FDA-cleared for ten general-surgery procedures) is the first credible soft-tissue challenger; Intuitive is ~30% down YTD with Q3 due late October (consensus revenue ~$2.9B; FY procedure growth guide 13.5–15.5%). U.S. procedure growth (12% in Q2) is the tell.

themes.title: Autonomy backlogs keep growing
themes.description: AeroVironment's backlog sits at a record $1.5B (1.4x book-to-bill) and Kratos grew revenue over 30% on its Valkyrie drone and laser lines — defense autonomy is one of the few robotics niches with immediate, funded demand.

themes.title: The humanoid supply chain is the safer bet
themes.description: Harmonic Drive's strain-wave reducers and Vishay Precision's sensors sit in the actuator bottleneck every humanoid maker has to solve, MP Materials' magnets underwrite it, and Nvidia's reported $12.9B Hugging Face deal plus Qualcomm's PickNik purchase show big silicon vendors buying the software layer.

tiers.label: Established / profitable
tiers.note: Diversified industrial, surgical and AI-infrastructure names where robotics is a real, disclosed business line but rarely the whole investment case.

bear_case.title: Humanoid valuations have outrun any plausible revenue
bear_case.description: Figure AI carries a ~$39B valuation on roughly 150 robots shipped in 2025; robotics VC funding is running near ~$56B in 2026 YTD against a market that's still mostly demos.

bear_case.title: Demos keep getting mistaken for autonomy
bear_case.description: Figure's Helix 2.5 reports 56% zero-shot success across unseen homes — meaning it fails nearly half the time — and Nucleus this week claimed a ~2-hour factory demo that is 'only' 60% autonomous. If a demo isn't labelled autonomous, assume teleoperation.

bear_case.title: Optimus's own maker has walked back its timeline twice
bear_case.description: Optimus' plant is ~40% through steel with limited production late 2027, Barron's (Oct 8) flagged limited operating evidence, and Musk is cutting AI5 memory just to get volume; timelines keep sliding.

bear_case.title: China's humanoid boom is drawing its own bubble warnings
bear_case.description: Unitree trades ~¥450 vs a ¥1,100 high, with BofA (¥350) and JPMorgan (¥300) both targeting below the market; Chatham House and China's NDRC have flagged frothy valuations across 150+ humanoid makers.

bear_case.title: Profitable names get cut anyway
bear_case.description: Symbotic is GAAP-profitable with a $22.5B backlog yet is down ~33% YTD and Barclays rates it Underweight ($38) — sentiment and fundamentals can diverge.

bear_case.title: Revenue today is still the boring parts of robotics
bear_case.description: Industrial automation, logistics automation and surgical robots generate real, recurring revenue now. Humanoids mostly don't yet — the investable robotics story and the humanoid hype story are not the same trade.

bear_case.title: Component suppliers carry customer-concentration risk of their own
bear_case.description: Vishay Precision's stock fell ~11% in a month on customer-concentration concerns even after a target upgrade tied to a humanoid design win — being 'picks and shovels' relocates single-customer risk rather than removing it.

bear_case.title: A crowded field guarantees a shakeout, not a winner
bear_case.description: 150+ companies chase humanoids, and prices are collapsing (Galbot ET1 from 79,000 yuan, Astribot T1 at $18,000). History says most of that capital won't be recovered.

bear_case.title: Teradyne's ~200% run leaves no cushion
bear_case.description: Shares swung from ~$449 to ~$403 in a week (once -9.8% on AI-capex worries); P/E >55 means a product-cycle stumble hurts far more than it would have a year ago — Watch.

bear_case.title: Capex gap: robots must earn their keep
bear_case.description: Tesla's 2026 capex tops $25B against $8.28B spent in H1 while Optimus shows no paying customers — investors are paying now for robot profits that are hard to measure.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Jetson Thor and Isaac GR00T keep it the default robotics compute stack, and it is reportedly weighing ~$1B more into Figure (Oct 8, unconfirmed); also in your AI, Quantum and Biotech sleeves — don't double-count.

positions.name: Rockwell Automation
positions.note: Shares +2.7% to ~$454 (~$50B cap) on Oct 2 as AI analytics and autonomous mobile robots roll out in biotech plants; the reshoring thesis is intact.

positions.name: Teradyne
positions.note: Gen 7 cobots and the Iris 100 launch are real, but ~$403 (down from ~$449 a week ago, P/S ~14, P/E >55) after a ~200% 12-month run still prices in the evidence — good business, wrong price.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: 'Project Swarm' magnet reservations underwrite humanoid actuator supply ahead of the Northlake, TX facility; also counts against your Critical Minerals sleeve.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: Record $1.5B backlog (+37% YoY) but shares slipped after the CCA award favored Kratos; also counts against your Defense sleeve.

positions.name: Symbotic
positions.note: GAAP-profitable with a $22.5B backlog (>30x quarterly revenue) and Walmart as anchor customer; ~$43 is ~45% below the $62.86 consensus target, though Barclays stays Underweight ($38) — held at core.

positions.name: Vishay Precision Group
positions.note: Its analyst target nearly doubled to $77 on a humanoid-vendor sensor design win, but shares have since pulled back ~11% on customer-concentration concerns — real optionality, kept small.

positions.name: Harmonic Drive Systems
positions.note: Makes the dominant strain-wave gear reducers that sit at the humanoid-actuator bottleneck, but its order book hasn't yet shown the consistent quarter-to-quarter conversion that would justify a larger position.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Engine read-through on Anduril's ~$5B CCA award and $2.08B backlog, but production needs FY27 funding — sized as optionality; also counts against your Defense sleeve.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.note: ~30% down YTD after J&J Ottava's FDA clearance; Q3 results due late October (consensus revenue ~$2.9B) — U.S. procedure growth (12% in Q2 vs 14% in Q1) decides whether this is timing or structural.

positions.name: Cognex
positions.note: Raised its through-cycle EBITDA margin target to 25–31% and is buying RealSense for $500M, but the stock is still digesting an HSBC downgrade — good business, unresolved near-term sentiment.

positions.name: Caterpillar
positions.note: Formalized a FieldAI physical-AI partnership on Sep 5, but robotics/autonomy remains a rounding error against Caterpillar's core equipment revenue and the adoption pace outside mining is unproven.

positions.name: Deere & Company
positions.note: Continues rolling out autonomous 9RX tractors and an autonomous commercial mower, but Deere discloses no standalone autonomy revenue — a slow-burn option on future automation, not a name to size around today.

positions.name: Fanuc
positions.note: Q1 net profit was up 35% and the new FANUC/Google Gemini 'AI Welding Agent' (engineering drawings straight to robot programs, shipping customers in December) is a genuine AI-native product, but shares are still below the average analyst target with earnings due Oct 22 (this week).

positions.name: ABB
positions.note: Selling its Robotics division to SoftBank for a $5.375B enterprise value simplifies the story but also removes robotics as an ABB-specific thesis until the deal — still awaiting regulatory clearance, expected mid-to-late 2026 — actually closes.

positions.name: Serve Robotics
positions.note: Q2 revenue grew 404% to $3.2M on 792 daily active robots, but FY26 revenue guidance was cut to $9–10M from $26M in the same release — real growth, but small and now less predictable.

positions.name: Johnson & Johnson
positions.note: Ottava got a flattering CNBC profile this month as J&J's entry into surgical robotics, but the system is still pre-commercial and robotics is immaterial to J&J's overall P&L — a name to watch for the surgical-robotics thesis, not to hold for it.

positions.name: Tesla
positions.note: Barron's (Oct 8) flagged limited Optimus operating evidence, shares ~$375 (Oct 13) ahead of Oct 21 earnings, and the plant is ~40% through steel with limited production late 2027 — years from revenue.

positions.name: Unitree Robotics
positions.note: Trading ~¥450 vs a ¥1,100 high with BofA (¥350) and JPMorgan (¥300) targeting well below the market; a US import ban also remains in force.
